title: Hotels Are Losing $135K a Year to Two Websites
hook_line: Independent hotels are handing away two-thirds of their bookings — and paying up to 30% commission to do it.
cliffhanger_line: Run the real numbers on a twenty-room hotel and that commission adds up to about $135,000 a year — gone, before the lights or the payroll are even paid.
pinned_comment: Full breakdown of where that money goes and how it gets clawed back — episode + blueprint linked in the description.
why: Opens on the two hardest numbers in the episode (63.4% loss, $135K/year) but stops before naming any fix, so the only way to find out what recovers the money is the long-form.

title: The Biggest Hospitality Funding Round Ever Just Landed
hook_line: In January 2026, a hotel software company raised $300 million — the largest round hospitality tech has ever seen.
cliffhanger_line: Mews now moves almost $20 billion a year through 15,000 hotels. Almost none of them are the twenty-room independent that actually needs this fixed.
pinned_comment: Who this money is actually built for — and who gets left out — in the full episode. Link in description.
why: Uses the funding scale as the surprise hook, then pivots to an unresolved tension (big platforms vs. small independents) without answering it — the resolution lives in long-form.

title: I Ran This Playbook With Fifty People. Most Hotels Have Zero.
hook_line: At the hotel I used to run, getting a guest from a social post to a booked room took a whole team. Most independent hotels don't have that team.
cliffhanger_line: I had fifty people on property to make that flow hold together. A bed-and-breakfast operator running the place alone has exactly one.
pinned_comment: What replaces the fifty-person team for a solo operator — full breakdown in the episode, link below.
why: A specific, personal anecdote creates curiosity about what stands in for the missing headcount without naming it — pure information gap, no resolution.

title: No Hotel Consultant Will Tell You Their Price
hook_line: Every company selling revenue management to independent hotels claims 5 to 15% more revenue. Not one of them will tell you what it costs.
cliffhanger_line: In a market where nobody prices in public, that silence is the finding — not a gap in the research.
pinned_comment: What that silence means for anyone trying to sell into this market — full episode and blueprint linked below.
why: Treats an industry-wide pricing blackout as the twist itself, ending on the observation rather than the strategy that exploits it, which is reserved for the full episode.
